prompt.brief: Design a real-time translation and localization service for text, speech, and documents across 100+ languages, with terminology control, context, quality estimation, and streaming output.
successSignals: Separate source text or media, locale and terminology policy, model versions, translation memory, quality scores, and published locale assets.
Route by language pair, domain, and latency class, stream speech segments, and keep terminology and protected names consistent.
Make translation requests idempotent, preserve segment boundaries and timestamps, and support human review for critical content.
Explain context windows, code switching, partial audio, glossary updates, privacy, fallback models, and cost controls.

functional: Translate text, speech, and documents, apply locale formatting and terminology, stream partial results, and return quality estimates.
Support language detection, glossary and translation-memory lookup, speaker timestamps, document layout, and human corrections.
Expose model and glossary versions, segment status, confidence, latency, usage, retention, and tenant access controls.
nonFunctional: Target p95 text translation latency below 200 ms for short segments and publish speech tokens with bounded lag.
Serve 100,000 segment requests per second across 100+ language pairs with language-specific pools and quotas.
Make segment requests, glossary publication, document jobs, and billing idempotent with stable source hashes.
Fall back to a general model or queued document translation when a language-specific model or terminology service fails.
scaleAssumptions: Support 100+ languages, 10 million text segments per hour, and 100,000 concurrent speech or document sessions.
Partition by tenant, language pair, domain, and session; isolate rare language pairs and long documents.
Retain encrypted source hashes, segment outputs, glossary versions, quality scores, and human corrections under policy.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Real-time translation commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Real-time translation writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Real-time translation version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Real-time translation by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Real-time translation work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Real-time translation projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Real-time translation projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Real-time translation records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Real-time translation latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
